correctness.rationale: For the exact stationary two-level Markov density, block integration yields an irreducible two-state chain with eigenvalue lambda in the mixing range, and conditional independent uniforms. A bounded martingale CLT establishes the knot variance v(1+lambda)/(1-lambda); conditional Donsker supplies independent pinned bridges. Dirichlet heat-kernel decomposition yields the exact supremum CDF. A Gaussian convex-set shift inequality plus positive tail shift mass proves strict CDF ordering; periodic and absorbing cases are handled separately by alternating labels and a conditional strong law. Standalone code was executed, reproducing normalization, independence Kolmogorov law, representative ordering and endpoint limit. Finite simulation does not certify the infinite-domain statements.

originality.rationale: The 2023/2024 source provides this copula and its mixing/spectral representation, and the 2009 weak-dependence empirical-process CLT covers existence of a Gaussian limit; both are openly acknowledged as prior. Detailed comparison to same-family full texts, weighted regime-residual KS results and relevant research findings did not locate the specific unweighted marginal supremum CDF integral, strict parameter-order law with testing implications, or periodic-versus-absorbing endpoint classification. The generic CLT is not misrepresented as new; historical priority is best-knowledge and provisional due to incomplete access to one plausible 2025 chapter.
residual_risks: 2025 type-I Longla copula handbook chapter doi:10.1016/bs.host.2025.01.006 lacked complete accessible text; its full content could conceivably contain some same-family testing result.
The proof assumes exact known uniform margins and copula parameters; fitted-model KS has a different limit.
Numerical heat-kernel quadrature is not a certified all-parameter error bound.
No independent audit or claim of exhaustive global literature uniqueness.

value.rationale: The ordinary two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov goodness-of-fit statistic has a universal null limit only under appropriate independence. For the natural two-state Markov copula example, the exact scalar integral gives a directly evaluable dependent-data null calibration, the strict persistence ordering shows which iid cutoffs are anticonservative or conservative, and exact periodic and absorbing endpoint laws distinguish ergodic dependence from loss of empirical-marginal consistency. This is a mathematically motivated complete classification, not an arbitrary finite example.
